newsitem.title: USA: Disney posts higher profits on growth in all units.
newsitem.headline: Disney posts higher profits on growth in all units.

text.p: Walt Disney Co. Tuesday reported better-than-expected fourth-quarter profits, reflecting record attendance at its theme parks, solid performance at the box office and improved results at its broadcasting division.

The Burbank, Calif.-based entertainment giant reported a pro forma profit of $354 million, or 52 cents a share, for the fiscal fourth quarter ended in September, up from $221 million, or 32 cents a share in the year-ago quarter. Pro forma revenues jumped 12 percent to $5.3 billion.

The pro forma results, which assume Capital Cities/ABC Inc. was part of Disney for both the most recent and the year-ago period, exceeded Wall Street's consensus estimate of 48 cents a share, sending Disney stock $2.75 higher to $76.25 on the New York Stock Exchange. Disney acquired Capital Cities/ABC last February.
Smith Barney analyst Jill Krutick said all three of Disney's divisions posted better-than-expected results in the quarter.

"The operating momentum showed across-the-board strength, from creative content to broadcasting to theme parks, and the current trends suggest that strength should continue," Krutick said. "The outlook looks very bright for Disney."

Indeed, with Disney's thriller "Ransom" already grossing more than $85 million in domestic box office and the live-action version of "101 Dalmatians" making its debut this week, industry experts predicted the first quarter of fiscal 1997 should continue to show solid results.
For the full year, pro forma net income increased 16 percent to $1.5 billion, and earnings per share increased 15 percent to $2.23.
Disney Chairman Michael Eisner said the improvement showed the company was successfully blending ABC operations with its existing studio and theme park business.

"I am extremely pleased with the progress we have made in integrating Disney and ABC," Eisner said in a statement. "The fact that we continued our strong growth during this period proves that the combined operations are working and working well."

Disney acquired Cap Cities/ABC for $19 billion in February, just as the network's ratings were starting to slide. The company made a number of moves aimed at boosting ratings,including the hiring of former NBC programming executive Jamie Tarses in June. But industry analysts said a turnaround at ABC will take time.

For the quarter, the broadcasting unit posted pro forma operating income of $229 million, up 36 percent from the year-ago quarter. However, most of that came from reductions in programme amortization costs.
David Londoner, analyst at Wertheim Schroder, estimated as much as $75 million of the unit's operating income in the quarter may have come from the accounting changes.
ABC's all-sports cable television network, ESPN, and the Disney Channel premium cable channel reported higher operating profits while profits at the ABC Network were slightly lower.

Disney said its theme parks had a banner quarter with revenues rising 11 percent to $1.2 billion and operating income up 16 percent to $242 million. For the fiscal year, theme park revenues increased 13 percent to $4.5 billion and operating income rose 15 percent to $990 million.

Creative Content, which includes Disney's motion picture studio operations, reported pro forma revenues for the quarter were up 18 percent to $2.7 billion and operating income was up 31 percent to $387 million.
For the fiscal year, the unit's revenues increased 17 percent to $10.5 billion while operating income of $1.6 billion was about equal to the prior-year performance.

Disney said Creative Content results for the quarter reflected the domestic home video releases of "Oliver & Company" and "Aladdin and the King of Thieves," the domestic box office success of "Phenomenon" and strong international theatrical performances by "The Rock" and "The Hunchback of Notre Dame."
Results for the quarter also reflected growth in international consumer products licensing.

On an as-reported basis, reflecting Capital City/ABC's results from the effective date of the acquisition on Feb. 9, Disney's revenues for the quarter increased 69 percent to $5.3 billion and operating income rose 73 percent to $858 million.
Net income increased 27 percent to $336 million and earnings per share decreased 2 percent to 49 cents a share.

For the fiscal year, revenues increased 54 percent to $18.7 billion, but net income fell to $1.21 billion from $1.38 billion. The 1996 results included two non-recurring charges during the second quarter -- a $300 million non-cash charge related to the implementation of an accounting change and a $225 million charge for costs related to the ABC acquisition.
Without the charge, net income rose to $1.53 billion from $1.38 billion.
